chapter: Billy Pierce Studio and New York tap
title: Their lifetime contract with Lucille Achet
summary: Pierce did not know the boys were under contract to Achet, who had the record shop and connections to record companies and theatre people.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Yes. Yeah, eventually, yes, he did. See, but he didn't realize that we were under contract, and we were supposed to eventually work as an act, you see.
You were under contract by whom?

With Lucille Achet, see. She was supposed to come up some -- maybe some while later, you know. She was maybe a year or so -- she was going to come up and join us, travel sometime with us, you know. See, we weren't just going to always stay in New York City, but New York City was like headquarters, you see. That came about after Nat Nazarro discovered us, you see.
So this contract that you had with Lucille, what was she doing to promote you in any way? What was your obligation? Was she trying to sell you as an act at that point?

Well, she was. That's what she does, you see, because she had the record shop there in Atlanta, Georgia, but I mean she was a very important woman. You understand? She's very popular. You see? I mean throughout the United States, you see, as a businesswoman, you see, and -- and through her father-in-Law, you know, and she was actually in the money world, you see, and important companies like record companies and so forth like that, theatrical people, she knew most of them, see? I mean --
